# Judith Chapter 10 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_010_page_001.jpg

---

**10:1** When Judith had finished crying out to the God of Israel and had completed all these words,

**10:2** she rose from where she lay on her face and called her maidservant and went down into the house. She took off the sackcloth and removed her widow's clothing.

**10:3** She bathed her body with water, anointed herself with rich myrrh, dressed her hair, set a tiara on her head, and put on the festive garments she had worn in the days of her husband Manasseh's life.

**10:4** She put sandals on her feet and adorned herself with ankle-rings, bracelets, rings, earrings, and all her jewelry, making herself as beautiful as possible in order to beguile the eyes of whatever men might see her.

**10:5** She gave her maidservant a skin of wine and a flask of oil, filled a pouch with roasted grain and cakes of dried figs and fine bread, wrapped all her provisions together, and loaded them on her.

**10:6** They went out to the gate of the city of Bethulia and found Uzziah standing there with the city elders, Chabris and Charmis.

**10:7** When they saw her — her face transformed and her clothing changed — they were utterly astonished at her beauty and said to her:

**10:8** "May the God of our ancestors grant you favor and fulfill your purpose, to the glory of the children of Israel and the exaltation of Jerusalem." Then she bowed in worship before God.

**10:9** She said to them, "Order them to open the city gate for me." They ordered the young men to open it, as she asked.

**10:10** They did so. Judith went out, she and her maidservant with her. The men of the city watched her until she had descended the mountain, crossed through the valley, and passed beyond their sight.

**10:11** As they were walking through the valley, an Assyrian patrol encountered them.

**10:12** They seized her and demanded, "What people do you belong to? Where have you come from, and where are you going?" She replied, "I am a Hebrew woman, and I am fleeing from before them, because they are about to be handed over to you as plunder.

**10:13** I am on my way to see Holofernes, the commander-in-chief of your army, to deliver true intelligence. I will show him the route by which he can advance and capture the entire hill country without the loss of a single man."

**10:14** When the men heard her words and looked at her face — for she was strikingly beautiful to their eyes — they said to her:

**10:15** "You have saved your life by coming down at once to present yourself to our lord. And now, go to his tent. Some of us will escort you until we hand you over to him.

**10:16** When you stand before him, do not be afraid — just tell him what you have told us, and he will deal with you generously."

**10:17** They selected a hundred men from their company to escort her and her maidservant, and they brought them to the tent of Holofernes.

**10:18** A commotion spread through the entire camp, for the news of her arrival traveled from tent to tent. They came and gathered around her as she stood outside the tent of Holofernes while his attendants were announcing her.

**10:19** They were astonished at her beauty, and they marveled at the Israelites because of her, each man saying to his neighbor, "Who could despise a people that has women like this? It would be foolish to leave a single man among them alive — if we let them go, they would be able to outwit the whole earth."

**10:20** Those who slept at Holofernes' side and all his attendants came out and led her into the tent.

**10:21** Holofernes was resting on his bed under a canopy woven of purple and gold, set with emeralds and precious stones.

**10:22** They reported her arrival to him and he came out to the anteroom, with silver lamps carried before him.

**10:23** When Judith came before him and before his attendants, they all marveled at the beauty of her face. She fell down before him on her face, and his servants raised her up.
